queries.details: Submission- and policy-level metadata for the quote request. Normalize all dates to the format YYYY-MM-DD.

entities.criteria: The CIBA quote / submission ID, usually in the subject line (e.g., 'Q00310033'). Return the CIBA quote number, not the broker's internal reference number.
Whether the submission is new business or a renewal, based on the email body (e.g., 'new business opportunity' = New; 'renewal we've handled', 'renewal of ours' = Renewal). Return 'New' or 'Renewal'.
The requested policy effective date, from the subject line or body. Return in the format YYYY-MM-DD. This is not the closing date.
The policy expiration date. Often the end of a term range (e.g., '07/09/2026 - 07/09/2027' -> 2027-07-09). Return in the format YYYY-MM-DD.
The date by which the broker needs the quote or authorization (e.g., 'Quote by date', 'provide authorization by'). Return in the format YYYY-MM-DD. Leave blank if not stated.
A short description of the insured's operations / occupancy as stated in the email (e.g., 'Apartments', 'Residential/Commercial', 'Condo association').

The named retail agent the submission is being handled on behalf of, when stated (e.g., 'for Drew Zadow', 'Trevor Sarsfield for Andrew Giordano'). This is a separate party from the broker who sent the email. Leave blank if not mentioned.

queries.details: Identity and address of the named insured / account. All fields refer to the insured, not the broker or carrier.

entities.criteria: The legal name of the named insured / account, including any DBA (e.g., 'GCP XXVIII Ltd DBA Park at Stone Oak'). This is the insured business, not the broker or carrier.
The named insured's mailing street address when stated in the email body. May differ from the physical / risk location.
The physical address(es) of the risk location(s) stated in the email body. Do not return 'See SOV', and any invalid address detail.
The city of the risk / insured location stated in the email.
The two-letter state code of the risk / insured location.
The county of the risk / insured location when stated (e.g., 'Coles County'). Leave blank if not mentioned.
The 5-digit or ZIP+4 postal code of the risk / insured location when stated.

queries.details: Extract policy and submission-level metadata for this submission.

entities.criteria: The consumer code id of the client, if available. This is not the agency customer id.
Policy effective date (ISO 8601, MM/DD/YYYY, or MM-DD-YYYY)
Two-letter primary / home state code for the policy

queries.details: All details of the broker who submitted the email: company, contact person, and brokerage address.

entities.criteria: The name of the wholesale brokerage / broker company that submitted the email (e.g., CRC Group, RT Specialty, McGowan Wholesale, Gallagher / AssuredPartners, Brown & Riding). Usually found in the sender's signature or email domain.
The email address of the broker who sent the email.
The direct, cell, or office phone number of the broker, from the email signature.
The broker's internal file or reference number for the submission when present (e.g., 'CRC#15374445', 'File # BR284499-01'). Do not return the CIBA quote number.
The primary street address line of the brokerage mentioned in the email (typically in the sender's signature). Do not extract a P.O. box; return the physical address.
The city of the broker's primary physical address mentioned in the email.
The two-letter state code of the broker's primary physical address mentioned in the email.
The ZIP / postal code of the broker's primary physical address mentioned in the email.

queries.details: Extract the producer / agent name. Both fields refer to the producer. The producer should be the person who sent the email from the broker company.

entities.criteria: First name of the producer / agent
Last name of the producer / agent

queries.details: Lines of insurance or coverage types a quote is being requested for. Include underlying structures, if available. Normalize all currency values to standard USD format. Convert k/m/b suffixes to full numbers, add $ and commas, and standardize negatives.

entities.criteria: The line of insurance / coverage type the quote is requested for (e.g., 'Property - Ground Up', 'Property - Multi Peril Other').

The requested coverage limit(s) for the line of business — the amount of insurance requested, including any layer / excess structure when given (e.g., '$10,000,000 per occurrence', '$49,657,125 xs $10M', '$10M primary'). This is NOT the same as TIV (total insurable value) or premium — do not put a TIV or premium figure here; leave blank if only a TIV/premium is stated and no coverage limit is given. Normalize currency to standard USD format.
The target, pure, or quoted premium for the line of business when stated (e.g., '$65,000 pure premium', '$5,000 - $7,500'). Normalize currency to standard USD format.

The carrier associated with the coverage when named - typically the incumbent / expiring carrier or the quoting market (e.g., 'Travelers', 'Programs Plus', 'Strata / Paragon'). Leave blank if not mentioned.
The date associated with the email at the time received. Return in the format YYYY-MM-DD.

queries.details: Property details per risk location. Return each address as a separate entry. Do not return an entry if there is no present street address line.

entities.criteria: Full street address line of the property, including the street number. Treat every distinct street number as a separate, unique address — do not merge, dedupe, or return one as a substitute for another (e.g. 118 ≠ 116 ≠ 140 ≠ 130 ≠ 111 ≠ 121, even on the same street). This is the street address only, not the location/building name or location number. Do not return 'See SOV', and any invalid address detail. This is not the city, state, or zip code.

The location (site) number for this row — from a 'Loc', 'Loc #', 'Location', 'Location #', or 'Premises #' column, or the LEFT-HAND portion of a combined 'Loc/Bldg' column.

- Compound values: take only the location portion. '2-3', '2.03', '2/3', '2 B', '002-003', 'Loc 2 Bldg 3' all yield '2'. The building portion belongs in Building Number.
- Strip labels and zero padding: 'Loc 4' -> '4', '004' -> '4'.
- In PDFs and Word documents the number often appears once beside a vertically merged cell or group heading spanning many rows. It applies to every row under that heading.
- If the schedule has no location numbering, number the groups sequentially in source order (1, 2, 3 ...), starting a new number wherever a new site or Location Name begins. Do not leave blank when grouping is discernible.
- Not unique. Consecutive rows sharing one value is the normal case.

Output ONLY the exact description string that best matches the property's use — do not output an ID number. Valid values (must match exactly, including punctuation and capitalization): 'Condominium/HOA', 'Commercial/Industrial', 'Commercial/Retail', 'Vacant Land', 'Commercial Storage Units', 'Habitational', 'Mixed Use - Condo', 'Mixed Use - Hab', 'Commercial/Warehouse', 'Parking Lot/Structure', 'Habitational-SFD DPLX', 'Commercial/Office'. Guidance: use 'Condominium/HOA' for residential condo associations/HOAs; 'Habitational' for apartments/multi-family rentals; 'Habitational-SFD DPLX' for single-family dwellings or duplexes; 'Mixed Use - Condo' when a mixed-use property is condo-owned; 'Mixed Use - Hab' when a mixed-use property is primarily residential rental; 'Commercial/Office' for office buildings; 'Commercial/Retail' for stores/shopping centers; 'Commercial/Industrial' for manufacturing/industrial facilities; 'Commercial/Warehouse' for warehouses/distribution; 'Commercial Storage Units' for self-storage facilities; 'Parking Lot/Structure' for parking facilities; 'Vacant Land' for undeveloped land. If uncertain between residential options, default to 'Habitational'.

Output ONLY the exact description string that matches the property's construction — do not output an ID number. Valid values (must match exactly, including punctuation and capitalization): 'ISO 1 - Wood Frame', 'ISO 2 - Joisted Masonry', 'ISO 3 - Noncombustible', 'ISO 4 - Masonry Noncombustible', 'ISO 5 - Modified Fire Resistive', 'ISO 6 - Fire Resistive', 'Not Available'. Guidance for mapping common source terms: 'ISO 1 - Wood Frame' for wood frame, frame, brick veneer over frame, or stucco over frame; 'ISO 2 - Joisted Masonry' for masonry/brick/concrete block exterior walls with wood/combustible floors or roof (also called ordinary construction or brick joisted); 'ISO 3 - Noncombustible' for unprotected steel frame with metal walls/roof (e.g., all-metal or steel buildings); 'ISO 4 - Masonry Noncombustible' for masonry or concrete block walls with noncombustible (metal/steel) floors and roof, common for warehouses, retail strips, and storage facilities; 'ISO 5 - Modified Fire Resistive' for protected steel or reinforced concrete with 1–2 hour fire ratings; 'ISO 6 - Fire Resistive' for protected structural steel or reinforced concrete with 2+ hour fire ratings, typical of high-rises. Only map to an ISO class when the source clearly indicates the construction; do not guess from building age, occupancy, or location. If the construction type is missing, ambiguous, or cannot be confidently classified, output exactly 'Not Available'

Output ONLY the exact description string that matches the property's housing type — do not output an ID number. Valid values (must match exactly, including punctuation and capitalization): 'Not Applicable', 'Assisted Living', 'Senior', 'Student', 'Market Rate', 'Non-Market Rent', 'Nursing Home', 'Single Room Occupancy (SRO)', 'Pending', 'Short Term Rental (STR)'. Guidance for classification: 'Assisted Living' when the source indicates assisted living, memory care, or residents receiving daily living support; 'Nursing Home' for skilled nursing, convalescent, or long-term medical care facilities; 'Senior' for age-restricted (55+/62+) or independent senior living communities without medical/assistance services; 'Student' for student housing, dormitories, or properties marketed to university students; 'Non-Market Rent' for affordable, subsidized, Section 8, LIHTC, rent-controlled, or income-restricted housing; 'Short Term Rental (STR)' for vacation rentals, Airbnb/VRBO-style operations, or units rented for under 30 days; 'Single Room Occupancy (SRO)' for SRO buildings, rooming/boarding houses, or units with shared kitchens/bathrooms; 'Market Rate' for standard apartments or rental housing at market rents with none of the above characteristics; 'Not Applicable' for non-residential properties (commercial, industrial, vacant land, parking) or any case where the housing type is unclear. Classify only from explicit evidence in the source (property name, description, or stated use); do not infer from location or building size alone. If unclear or not stated, output exactly 'Not Applicable'.
The total insurable value (TIV) of the building or property. If unclear, use the total TIV of the whole building across all entries.
The specified number of locations associated with the property.
